answer: A farm scripting its whole fleet fires them together, so that the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 249 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The canyon detector writes to opal, and timber makes public every merge. Submissions that land within 271 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 10 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
